_readme: Identity merges applied by build-company-base.py on every rebuild. Three sources of duplication on this investor: (a) the firm renamed the company and both renderings survive across site eras; (b) the 2002-2006 LOGO-ONLY era named rows from the company's own domain or its logo filename, so the same company appears under a stem and under its rendered name; (c) the Form D sweep found the company's LEGAL entity name while the site carried its brand. Every group was judged in the grind and the reasoning is on the non-canonical row's classification note.

ERIK'S RULING, 2026-09-06: merge. Cyanogen Inc (the commercial CyanogenMod distribution, backed by Redpoint in 2013) shut its consumer business in December 2016, kept the cyngn.com domain and renamed to CYNGN Inc, which now trades on NASDAQ as CYN — one company across one rename, not two. The base carried both because the 2015-2019 cards listed 'Cyanogen' while the 2020 card listed 'CYNGN' with the same link and the same 'Series A in 2013' claim.
